messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PD#78912 — infra-db "connection-pool-exhaustion"  (severity: P1). Threshold: pg_connections > 950 for 2m. Link: https://pagerduty.example/alerts/78912

pagerduty-bot: auto-ack attempted: no on-call responded in first 30s, escalating to secondary.

sre-raj: acked: I'm on it — grabbing console + psql. Observed high active connections on writer: 1023, pg_stat_activity shows many idle in transaction + long-running COPYs.

infra-amy: seeing correlated spike in Redis rejects (ERR maxclients) around same time. Could be a cascade: slow writes -> retries -> Redis fanout.

carla-dbe: @sre-raj can you paste `SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state <> 'idle';` results? Also check pgbouncer stats.

sre-raj: pastebin of quick commands: ```
-- on primary
SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state <> 'idle'; -- 416
SELECT pid, usename, query_start, now() - query_start AS duration, query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state <> 'idle' ORDER BY duration DESC LIMIT 10;
-- pgbouncer stats
SHOW POOLS; SHOW STATS;```

ben-backend: I'm seeing a deployment earlier today that increased parallel batch writes to 50 -> 200 workers in one service. Rolling it back now (deploy revert in progress). Could be hammering DB.

carla-dbe: Noted long-running COPY from service-user — that's the top offender holding connections for minutes. We should kill it if it's a retry loop.

sre-raj: I killed 3 queries from that user (pids 12456/12457/12458). Connections dropped to ~710, but still above safe threshold (target < 600).

oncall-rotation: @infra-amy start pgbouncer emergency scaling? We can temporarily increase pool_size and max_client_conn, but need a graceful plan.

infra-amy: pgbouncer scale: nodepool autoscaling hit limit in us-west-2. I can bump max_client_conn on pgbouncer config but that risks OOM on a single pool host. Alternative: enable read-only routing for heavy endpoints to replicas.

carla-dbe: Recommend short term: 1) roll back the batch worker change (ben rolling back). 2) reduce app DB pool_size to 20 via feature flag. 3) set pgbouncer to reject new long transactions: increase statement_timeout for ephemeral users. Also preparing a runbook step: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/db-conn-waterfall

ben-backend: rollback completed, traffic reduced ~35% within 2m. We also toggled a runtime flag to limit concurrency to 25.

incident-bot: PagerDuty update: alert status changed to acknowleged by sre-raj. Escalation paused.

sre-raj: after kills + rollback, active non-idle connections down to 412. Application error rate dropped from 6% -> 1.2%. Latency improved from 750ms p50 -> 230ms.

infra-amy: Redis side: we had a hot-key eviction pattern causing CPU spikes on primary replica; spun up an additional replica and enabled replica promotion stabilization. Replica lag peaked 180s, now ~12s behind.

carla-dbe: We're still seeing intermittent pgbouncer queueing because some sessions are stuck in idle-in-transaction state. I'm running a short script to terminate idle-in-transaction older than 30s for non-critical roles: ```
-- careful: kills only test/test-worker roles
SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state = 'idle in transaction' AND now() - xact_start > interval '30 seconds' AND usename LIKE 'worker_%';
```

oncritical-note: We will not terminate sessions for replication/monitoring users.

sre-raj: Ran the script, cleared ~48 stuck sessions. pgbouncer free_clients increased, backlog cleared.

oncall-rotation: Customer impact assessment: internal dashboards show ~1200 requests failing in last 10m, mostly non-critical sync jobs and some realtime edits (~3% of write traffic). No major data corruption reported. Logging retention wise, we've captured relevant traces: trace IDs added to incident page.

ben-backend: Feature flags to throttle non-urgent background jobs have been enabled across the fleet. That reduced sustained DB load by another ~20%.

carla-dbe: Next steps (short-term): 1) add a temporary statement_timeout for job-user to 60s, 2) patch app to use COPY in smaller batches, 3) schedule DB maintenance window to tune pgbouncer per-app pools.

infra-amy: Long-term action items: revisit autoscaling policy for pgbouncer nodes, add proactive throttling on our write-heavy endpoint, and improve observability: correlate pgbouncer wait_count -> app feature flags.

incident-bot: Incident note: PD#78912 acknowledged at 1741239999 by sre-raj. PagerDuty: incident annotated with mitigation steps and runbook link.

sre-raj: Marking for handoff in 30m to next on-call. I'll leave a summary in the incident tracker and handoff to @oncall-rotation.

oncall-rotation: I have the handoff, monitoring for 2h. Will validate replica promotion behavior and ensure no recurrence. If queues rise > 600 active we re-open page.

carla-dbe: Postmortem action items tracking: https://redwood.internal/pm/INC-78912 — owners assigned: pgbouncer infra (infra-amy), backend throttling (ben-backend), DB query patterns (carla-dbe).

sre-raj: closing notes: key root cause: unbounded batch worker increase + a few long-running transactions + pgbouncer scaling limits -> connection waterfall. Resolved with rollback, connection cleanup, temporary throttles, and Redis replica addition.

pagerduty-bot: PD#78912 resolved by sre-raj at 1741241450.

incident-bot: auto-summary generated: "DB connection pool exhaustion triggered by surge in parallel batch workers leading to cascading rejects in Redis; mitigations: worker rollback, kill stuck queries, pgbouncer tuning, spawn Redis replica, throttle background jobs." Tags: db, redis, pgbouncer, pagerduty, oncall
